channel.description: Single Audit findings, corrective action plans and the Uniform Guidance, in plain English.

item.title: How to write a corrective action plan that actually closes a Single Audit finding
item.description: What 2 CFR 200.511 requires in a corrective action plan, who writes it, and why plans that promise to "strengthen controls" keep turning into repeat findings.

item.title: Material weakness vs significant deficiency: what the label on your finding means
item.description: The three kinds of Single Audit findings, how auditors grade control problems, and why a material weakness costs more than its wording suggests.

item.title: The 5 C's of audit findings: how to read your finding the way your auditor wrote it
item.description: Criteria, condition, cause, effect and corrective action. What each element of an audit finding means, and why "cause: oversight" is never the real cause.

item.title: What is a Single Audit finding? A plain-English guide for nonprofit leaders
item.description: A Single Audit finding is a documented gap between what the federal rules require and what your organization did. Here is how to read one, part by part.
